- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:249 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The one-pass whitespace, invisible-character, whitespace strip does not loop, so a body starting `\u200c \u200d<!-- check-failure-triage:fp=... -->` keeps U+200D before `<!--` and the anchored `re.match` fails. Other invisible format characters (U+200E/U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2061-U+2064, U+00AD, U+034F) are not covered either.
  WHY: Line 250 prints `skip` for the label-stripped triage issue, so it takes the default-branch path instead of being refused as `label_missing`. The reviewer notes there is no privilege escalation, because exploiting it needs a deliberately edited body.
- Hardening suggestion: replace the three chained strips with one anchored `re.sub` over a character class, then split on the first newline (about 2 lines changed). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:~249 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The chained `lstrip` handles one run of whitespace, one of invisibles and one of whitespace, so for `\u200c \u200d<!-- ... -->` U+200D survives and `re.match(r"<!--\s*check-failure-triage:", first_line)` returns None. The same happens for `\u200c\n\u200d` and `\u200c\t\u200d`.
  WHY: A label-stripped triage issue is treated as an ordinary issue and gets the default branch instead of failing closed with `label_missing`. The existing fixture `prose_marker_header_behind_zero_width_joiner_refuses` covers only adjacent invisibles, so the interleaved case is unverified.
- Hardening suggestion: add a `LEADING_NOISE_RE` anchored regex to replace the chained lstrip, and add an interleaved-prefix fixture expecting exit 3 with `label_missing`, parameterised into PROSE_MARKER_FIXTURES (about 3 lines plus one new fixture file). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:249-250 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The chained `lstrip()` calls do not remove invisible characters when whitespace separates them; a body beginning `\u200c \u200d<!-- check-failure-triage:fp=... -->` keeps U+200D before the marker.
  WHY: The earlier marker search finds the header, but the first-line `re.match` fails on the remaining U+200D, so the skip branch accepts this label-less triage issue as ordinary instead of refusing it as `label_missing`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:249 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The chained `lstrip()` calls handle only three leading runs, so for U+200C + space + U+200D before the marker the second strip removes U+200C, the third removes the space, and U+200D remains, making `re.match` at line 250 return None.
  WHY: The prose-marker skip (lines 250-252) prints `skip`, so `resolve_ci_triage_branch` falls through to the default branch instead of `refuse label_missing`. The new fixture `prose_marker_header_behind_zero_width_joiner_refuses.json` covers only adjacent invisibles.
- Hardening suggestion: the fixed strip set also excludes U+200E/U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2061-U+2064, U+00AD and U+034F. Replace the three chained `lstrip()` calls with one anchored `re.sub` over a wider character class and extend the fixture to cover a whitespace-invisible-whitespace prefix (about 2 lines changed).
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
